thread:
anya: Canary run for mt-xxl on L40S fp8 kernel showed a reproducible BLEU drop, small repro attached. Anyone seen a residual/activation scaling leak like this before?

liam: Which quant pipeline did you use (AWQ/GPTQ/our fp8 autotune)? and what's the exact BLEU delta?

anya: Using our fp8-autotune branch (kernel v2.3). Config: channelwise scale, block=128, no per-channel clipping. Command: `runcanary --model mt-xxl --kernel fp8-l40s --seq 1024 --batch 8 --quant-mode fp8-autotune`
Baseline (fp16): BLEU=35.4
FP8 canary: BLEU=29.2 (-6.2)
Perp: fp16=3.8 fp8=6.5

anya: Quick diff: forcing FP16 on all FFN layers -> BLEU=34.8 (so FFN quantization looks like the main culprit).

todd: That's a huge regression localized to FFNs. Any signs of activations saturating or NaNs during generation?

anya: No NaNs, but we see large clamp hits in the runtime logs. Snippet:```
[2026-03-18T11:02:12Z] fp8_kernel: layer ffn_21 max_act=9.83 scale=0.012 clamp_hits=1423
[2026-03-18T11:02:12Z] fp8_kernel: layer ffn_22 max_act=10.1 scale=0.011 clamp_hits=1548
```
These layers also have much higher quantization error in the offline MSE probes.

liam: Hm. On L40S we added a different prefix-fusion path that skips the residual pre-scale handshake in some fast paths. Could be the new kernel not applying residual scaling before quantization, so FFN outputs clip more often.

liam: Try a quick canary where you enable `--force-residual-handshake` or set `runtime.fp8.safe_clip=true` and re-run. If BLEU recovers, we have a handshake bug in the L40S fast path.

anya: I ran `--force-residual-handshake` and BLEU improved to 33.9 (still -1.5 from fp16). With `runtime.fp8.safe_clip=true` BLEU=34.6. So safe_clip helps a lot.

anya: Minimal repro patch:```
# hacky local patch applied to kernel v2.3
if layer.is_ffn and kernel_path=="l40s_fastpath":
    apply_residual_handshake(output, pre_ln_scale)
```
results: BLEU=34.8 (close to fp16).

todd: Looks like two issues: handshake missing in the fastpath + slightly different scale estimation in our autotuner for those FFN weight shapes. Both contribute. We should avoid enabling fp8 kernel on mt-xxl until we: 1) fix handshake, 2) tune per-layer scale heuristics for large FFNs.

infra-bot: :warning: Canary deployment to group l40s-canary-3 rolled back automatically (policy: quality-drop >= 4 BLEU) at 11:32 UTC. Reason: metric delta -6.2.

anya: Logging/telmetry follow-ups: add per-layer `clamp_hits` and `scale_estimation` to the canary export. Also emit an `overflow_rate` gauge (count of clamp_hits / tokens). I'll open a ticket.

dev-bot: Created ticket ML-7832: "L40S fp8 fastpath missing residual handshake + per-layer scale variance" assigned to @liam.

liam: I'll add a targeted unit test that parallels the l40s_fastpath and checks that pre-residual scaling is applied (and an integration canary with `safe_clip` toggles). Also add a fallback in the router: avoid enabling fp8 for models with FFN peak-act>9 until we've tuned scales.

anya: Action items:
- liam: fix handshake + add unit test (ETA EOD 3/19)
- anya: extend canary telemetry + run a smaller-batch canary (batch 2) to see whether batching masks the issue (ETA 3/19 AM)
- todd: coordinate a temp block in the rollout matrix for mt-xxl on L40S until patch lands

liam: FYI this one explains why earlier FP8 canaries on H100 didn't regress as much — H100 fastpath includes the handshake. L40S optimized path accidentally skipped it when we merged the fusion patch.

anya: I'll post the reproduced logs and the patch diff to ML-7832. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
